name: Methane leak detection and repair (LDAR, satellites and continuous monitoring)
aliases: Methane leak detection (OGI cameras, satellites, continuous sensors)
applications: finding and fixing methane leaks at wells, compressors and processing plants
principle: Leaks are located by surveying facilities with optical gas imaging cameras, aircraft or drone sensors, fixed continuous sensors or satellites, and then quantified and repaired. Satellites flag large emission events and recurrent leaks, which are passed to operators for rapid repair. A repeat survey confirms the fix.

performance.metric: fossil-fuel methane emissions that could be avoided at no net cost
performance.basis: about 35 Mt; at average 2024 energy prices; oil and gas share higher than coal

performance.metric: methane emitted by the fossil fuel sector
performance.basis: abatement could have made nearly 100 bcm of gas available

performance.metric: satellites in orbit able to observe methane emissions
share of satellite-detected oil and gas sources that were recurrent
performance.basis: Carbon Mapper analysis of more than 2,000 plumes

source.note: IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, 2025 assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Periodic methane emission monitoring in oil and gas facilities' 9; 'Satellite-based methane emission monitoring in oil and gas facilities' 9

advantages: Many measures pay for themselves from the gas recovered
Satellites cover remote and offshore areas
Strong regulatory trend towards required LDAR
limitations: Satellites struggle in overcast and high-latitude regions
Dispersed small sources are a large share of basin emissions
